#image("/imgs/ap-calc-bc-2019-frq-03-diagram-01.jpg", width: 65%)

Graph of $f$

The continuous function $f$ is defined on the closed interval $- 6 <= x <= 5$. The figure above shows a portion of the graph of $f$, consisting of two line segments and a quarter of a circle centered at the point $(5 \,3)$. It is known that the point ( $3 \,3 - sqrt(5)$ ) is on the graph of $f$.

(a) If $integral_(- 6)^(5) f(x) d x = 7$, find the value of $integral_(- 6)^(- 2) f(x) d x$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

(b) Evaluate $integral_(3)^(5)lr((2 f'(x)+ 4)) d x$.

(c) The function $g$ is given by $g(x)= integral_(- 2)^(x) f(t) d t$. Find the absolute maximum value of $g$ on the interval $- 2 <= x <= 5$. Justify your answer.

(d) Find $lim_(x -> 1) frac(10^(x)- 3 f'(x),f(x)- arctan x)$.
